name: Average Basics: Sum, Count and Missing Values
description: Understand average as an equal share, move between average and total, and solve simple missing-value questions.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's core rule Average = Sum of observations / Number of observations. Build the inverse forms Sum = Average × Number and Number = Sum / Average. Use direct lists, unknown observations, symbolic averages and simple equations such as finding the other number when the average of two is known. Include the objective patterns where every observation is increased by the same amount or multiplied by the same factor, showing that the mean changes in the same way. Use simple checks by reconstructing the total from the final average. A learner should be able to translate an average statement into a total immediately, recover one missing value, and distinguish the number of observations from the sum. Keep subgroup weighting and membership changes for later subtopics.

name: Consecutive and Patterned Averages
description: Find averages of natural numbers, multiples, consecutive numbers, odd/even sequences and selected values in an interval.
script_scope: Teach the sequence patterns used throughout the chapter's solved examples and objective questions. Cover the average of the first n natural numbers using n(n+1)/2, the first n multiples of a number, consecutive integers, consecutive odd/even numbers, and equally spaced lists where the mean is the central value or midpoint of the endpoints. Include finding the average of numbers in an interval that satisfy a condition, such as divisible numbers or listed primes, by first identifying the correct observations. Include the book's common traps: counting endpoints incorrectly, using all numbers in the interval instead of only qualifying numbers, and confusing the sum with the average. A learner should be able to exploit symmetry instead of adding long lists when the pattern allows it.

name: Weighted and Frequency Averages
description: Compute averages when values occur different numbers of times or carry different weights.
script_scope: Teach weighted average as total weighted value divided by total weight. Use the chapter's patterns of quantities bought at different prices, groups with different counts, frequency tables, and examinations where some subjects or exams have larger weights. For grouped working-hour intervals, use the class midpoint as the representative working hours exactly as the chapter solution does, then multiply midpoint by number of employees. Make clear why simply averaging subgroup means is only valid when their weights are equal. Include recovering an unknown weighted component. A learner should be able to create a value × weight table mentally or on paper, total the weighted values, total the weights, and divide once at the end.

name: Combined Groups and Group Ratios
description: Combine group averages and work backward to find group sizes, ratios or percentages.
script_scope: Teach combined-average questions for two or more groups: convert each group mean to a group total, add totals and counts, and divide. Work backward when the combined mean is known to find an unknown group mean or group size. Teach the chapter's ratio/alligation pattern for two groups: if their means are H and L and the combined mean is M, the group-size ratio is (M-L):(H-M), with the sides mapped carefully to the opposite differences. Use boys/girls, technicians/non-technicians, passed/failed and experienced/inexperienced patterns from the objective section. Convert a ratio to percentages when asked. Include a three-group example where one intermediate combined average reveals a group ratio. A learner should be able to tell when a combined average determines a unique ratio and avoid taking an unweighted mean of subgroup means.

name: Missing, Overlapping and Partial Averages
description: Use totals to recover hidden observations when subsets overlap or only part of a list is described.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's repeated pattern Sum = Average × Count for partial groups. Cover a middle observation found from the average of all items plus averages of the first and last parts; overlapping first-k and last-k groups where one observation is counted twice; pairwise averages such as A+B, B+C and A+C; finding the mean of an unmentioned remainder; and comparing two overlapping windows of days or scores. Include the data-sufficiency idea seen in the objective section: translate each average statement into a sum equation and decide whether the target is uniquely determined before calculating. A learner should be able to draw or list which observations are included in each subtotal so they do not double-count or subtract the wrong group.

name: Adding, Removing, Replacing and Correcting Observations
description: Track how an average changes when members enter, leave, are replaced, or when recorded data is corrected.
script_scope: Teach changes to a data set through totals. For adding a member, compare old total nA with new total (n+1)B; for removing a member, subtract the new total from the old total; for replacement with the same count, use change in total = count × change in average, which equals new value − old value. Cover groups entering/leaving and average of the group removed. Teach correction of wrong entries by repairing the total: corrected total = recorded total − wrong value + correct value, including two-error cases and percentage error in a reported mean. Reinforce the objective pattern that if every observation is raised by k, the mean rises by k, and if all are multiplied by c, the mean is multiplied by c. A learner should be able to identify whether the count changes before choosing the equation.

name: Age Averages Through Time
description: Solve average-age problems involving years passing, family changes, births, teachers and replacements.
script_scope: Teach age-average questions as total-age questions. When the same group remains intact, each person gains the same number of years, so the group's average rises by that many years. Use this to move totals between past and present. Cover a teacher or instructor joining a class, one person leaving or being replaced, children being born, a son or daughter-in-law joining a family, and multi-stage family timelines at the level represented by the chapter. Show months-to-years conversion when an average changes by months. Use a simple vertical timeline so the learner keeps group size and elapsed years visible. A learner should be able to update both total age and number of people at each event instead of merely adding years to an old average when membership changes.

name: Average Rates, Prices and Productivity
description: Handle average price, buying rate, work rate and other cases where the denominator itself changes.
script_scope: Teach the objective patterns where a rate is itself a quotient, so blindly averaging the displayed rates can be wrong. Cover equal quantities bought at different kg-per-rupee rates by finding total quantity and total money; equal money spent at different prices per litre by finding litres bought each time; workers who take different minutes per unit by converting each to units per minute before averaging productivity; average visitor or charge rates when different day types have different counts; and a fixed-plus-variable boarding-expense pattern where average expense per person changes with group size. Keep the method source-grounded: convert each rate statement back into an actual total numerator and denominator, combine those totals, then form the requested average.

name: Cricket, Scores and Changing Performance Averages
description: Use averages in innings, run rates, bowling figures and examination-score changes.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's performance-average patterns. Cover a batsman's score in the next innings when his average rises or falls; highest and lowest innings removed from an overall average; a run-rate target where earlier overs are already completed; a captain's score compared with the average of the other batsmen; bowling average as runs conceded per wicket and how a new spell changes it; and examination-paper average changes caused by extra marks. The unifying method is to convert every average or rate into a total, make the described change, then divide by the new count if needed. A learner should be able to distinguish the old count from the new count and avoid applying the average increase directly to a single score.

name: Average Speed for Equal Distances
description: Understand and use the chapter's special average-speed formula for equal outward and return distances.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's stated formula for a journey covering equal distances at x km/h and y km/h: average speed = 2xy/(x+y). Derive it with a small equal-distance example by adding journey times, so the learner sees why (x+y)/2 is generally wrong for equal distances: the slower part takes longer. Practice direct substitution, return journeys, simplifying the fraction, and checking that the answer lies between the two speeds and is pulled toward the slower speed. State the condition clearly: this shortcut is for equal distances. If the distances are not equal, the learner must return to total distance divided by total time rather than force the shortcut.
